author: vreich-ui
body:
The client-connection variables have now been wiped twice by a release. Root cause is not that anyone forgot a warning — it is that the command people copy was itself the destructive one.

## What was actually wrong

`docs/platform/PHASE4_RUNBOOK.md` step 2 deployed with `--set-env-vars` / `--set-secrets`, which REPLACE a service's entire environment with only what is passed. That command listed the four store/CORS variables, so every release silently deleted the six client-connection variables (`DR_LURIE_*`, `PDF_TOOL_*`, `PLATFORM_*` endpoint + token). All client connections then fail closed with "endpoint is not configured" **while `repository.get_health` stays green**, because workspace state lives in GCS and is independent of the revision. It reads as a credentials problem and never is one.

A warning was added under that command last time. It did not help, because the copy-pasteable command was still wrong. This changes the command.

There is also no CI/CD for the MCP image — `cloudbuild.mcp.yaml` only builds it — so "merged" and "deployed" diverge by default, and nothing was checking the second fact. A revision serving pre-R-3 code was mistaken for the merged one for hours, with health green throughout.

## What ships

**`scripts/deploy-mcp.sh`** — one committed release command, so the correct flags are not something to remember:

- `--update-env-vars` / `--update-secrets` (merge) instead of `--set-*` (replace), so anything already on the service survives untouched;
- image tagged with the git SHA rather than `latest`, which is what makes "which commit is live?" answerable at all;
- refuses a dirty working tree unless confirmed, since the tag would otherwise not describe what is in the image;
- prints the serving revision's full environment after deploying, so a missing variable is visible immediately;
- then runs the verifier below.

**`scripts/verifyDeployment.ts`** (`npm run verify:deploy`) — the check that would have caught both incidents, in one command:

| Check | Catches |
|---|---|
| `tools/list` from the live endpoint, fingerprinted and hashed exactly as the two-plane drift detector does, compared to the committed `docs/mcp-tool-manifest.json` | a stale revision — health checks structurally cannot detect this | | `project_list` through the same endpoint, reporting endpoint/token configuration per project, naming the missing variables | a wiped environment |

Read-only: `tools/list` and `project_list` only. `readManifest` is now exported from `twoPlaneDrift.ts` so the live check and the CI lock compare against the same committed artifact rather than two ideas of it.

**Runbook commands corrected at the source:**

- PHASE4 (service) — now `--update-*`, with `--set-*` explicitly reserved for first-time creation, plus a verification section and a pointer to the script.
- PHASE2 (conductor job) — same substitution; the job had the identical trap.
- PHASE1 — left as `--set-*` because it *creates* the job, where there is nothing to preserve, with a note not to copy the flags into a later update.
- Removing a single variable later: `--remove-env-vars KEY`. Never re-list everything with `--set-*` to drop one key; that is the original bug.

## Verification of the current deployment

Checked live before writing any of this, on revision `cms-agent-mcp-00028-8f4`:

- `platform` → `Platform_MCP_Server` 0.1.0
- `dr-lurie` → `Dr_Lurie_MCP_Server` 0.1.0
- `pdf-tool` → `pdf-tool-agent-artifacts` 0.2.0

And the merged code is confirmed live **by function rather than by assumption**: a stringified schema sent to `workspace_update_node_output_schema` was accepted, which only post-R-3 code does. The probe deliberately sent `article_body`'s own existing schema back, so it was a no-op in content; workspace v84 → v85 with the reason recorded in the ledger.

`SESSION_HANDOFF.md` §2 is rewritten accordingly — it had been left saying the connections were down.

Suite unchanged and green: 806 root / 88 ui, both typechecks, all three CI locks. The new scripts were exercised for their failure paths (missing env → exit 2, unreachable endpoint → exit 1, `bash -n` clean); the success path needs the live URL and bearer, which this sandbox does not hold.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #751 — ocean-crossing was gated exactly once, for `transport` only, via
`unit.type === 'transport'` checks duplicated in two movement modules. Every
other naval unit (17 more player types, all 6 pirate hulls, plus a legendary
beast) has always been free to enter `ocean` tiles the instant it exists,
including era-1 Galley.

- **Data model:** new `UnitDefinition.waterAccess` / `PirateHullDefinition.waterAccess`
  (`'coastal' | 'ocean'`), classified on every naval unit and pirate hull, with a
  catalog-coverage test that fails loudly if a future naval unit omits it.
- **Movement:** both duplicated checks collapse into one shared `canHullEnterOcean()`
  predicate. The old `galleys`/`celestial-navigation` movement-time tech gate is
  retired — ocean access is now a permanent hull property. Coastal-only forever:
  Galley, Transport. Everything else (Trireme onward, all pirate hulls from
  `pirate_frigate` up) is ocean-going.
- **Tech tree:** `celestial-navigation` is repurposed from a movement gate (that was
  false for everyone but Transport) into a production prerequisite on the first
  ocean-going unit in each line (`navigation`, `triremes`, `colonial-trade`).
- **Content honesty:** Galley/Trireme descriptions now state their water access
  directly; the retired "Units can cross ocean" phrase is denylisted so it can't
  resurface.
- **Save migration (schema 8 → 9):** any existing save with a now-coastal-only hull
  sitting on `ocean` gets it relocated to the nearest coast via deterministic BFS
  (with a deletion fallback if none is reachable, and collision-avoidance so two
  stranded units — even different owners — can never land on the same tile).
  Cargo follows its Transport. A per-owner notification is logged, scoped so it
  never leaks across civs in hot-seat.
- **Two live gaps found and fixed in final review** (not just documented as
  residual risk): journey automation's path-planning was hull-blind in both
  `main.ts` and `turn-manager.ts` (fixed by threading unit context into `findPath`,
  same as every other caller already does); and the save migration's destination
  search could collide two different units onto one tile (fixed with an occupied-set
  guard).

**Deliberately out of scope, documented rather than silently dropped:** a
coastal-only UI badge on unit cards. The existing generic blocked-move
notification already gives real player feedback the moment a move is attempted,
so this is a discoverability polish item, not a functional gap — reasonable to
follow up separately per this repo's incremental-mr-completion convention.

**Also flagged, not fixed here:** a one-off connectivity check (BFS-based, not
committed as a permanent test) found that the map generator gives no guarantee
of a coast-only path between separate landmasses — 19/19 multi-landmass
map/seed combinations tested had at least one disconnected pair. Combined with
coastal-only hulls, this means an explorer-style player can plausibly be
unable to reach a second landmass until Carrack (era 2). This is a
map-generator question, not a naval-rules bug, and needs its own decision
(accept as pacing, or file a follow-up) — flagged for the maintainer rather
than expanding this PR's scope.

Full design rationale (including a real correction mid-review — the initial
historical framing for the coastal/ocean boundary overstated its case, and the
spec was rewritten to say so plainly) is in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-naval-water-class-design.md`, with the
task-by-task implementation plan in
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-naval-water-class-plan.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test` — full suite (436 files / 7032 tests) green
- [x] `yarn build` — clean
- [x] New `tests/systems/naval-water-class.test.ts` — hull classification catalog
      coverage (player + pirate), movement enforcement (coastal blocked / ocean
      allowed, both player and pirate hulls, plain-language message check), tech-tree
      prerequisite wiring
- [x] `tests/storage/save-migrations.test.ts` — relocation, cargo-follows, deletion
      fallback, hot-seat notification scoping, no-collision-on-relocation
- [x] `tests/core/turn-manager.test.ts` — journey automation respects hull class;
      verified this test fails without the `turn-manager.ts` fix before confirming
      it passes with it
- [x] Regression sweep — every pre-existing fixture that placed a now-coastal-only
      hull on an all-ocean test map (found via full-suite runs, not guessed at)
      updated to use an ocean-going substitute or the new blocker code
- [x] Targeted rerun of `pacing-audit`, `pacing-reference-economy`,
      `world-pressure-fairness` — unaffected, as expected for a non-yield change

body:
## Summary

Adds the missing `IndexDeltaDeclaration(version=40, ...)` entry to `polylogue/storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py`'s `INDEX_DELTA_DECLARATIONS` registry so `devtools lab policy schema-versioning` recognizes the index-tier v39→v40 schema bump.

## Problem

`devtools lab policy schema-versioning` was failing on master: "undeclared index schema deltas found: 1, missing: [40]". PR #3068 ("bind query_units continuations to the archive epoch", polylogue-z9gh.9) bumped `INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION` from 39 to 40 -- adding the `query_unit_frame_state` table plus its insert/update/delete triggers on `session_links`, `sessions`, `messages`, `blocks`, `session_tags`, `session_profiles`, and `delegation_facts` -- but never added the matching `IndexDeltaDeclaration`. `INDEX_DELTA_DECLARATIONS` jumped straight from `version=39` to `version=41` (the latter added by a later, unrelated PR for polylogue-2i2w), silently skipping 40.

## Solution

Added `IndexDeltaDeclaration(version=40, classes=(DerivedDeltaClass.INDEX_ONLY,), operations=(...))` describing the actual v40 delta: one `FastForwardOperation` (`kind=REPLACE_TABLE`) whose `objects` list the `query_unit_frame_state` table and all 21 `query_unit_frame_*` triggers, matching exactly what df8683767 (#3068) added to `INDEX_DDL`. No canonical DDL, executor, or runtime behavior changes -- this is a declaration-only fix; the schema itself already exists and is deployed.

## Verification

- `devtools lab policy schema-versioning` before: `undeclared index schema deltas found: 1` / `missing: [40]`; after: `undeclared index schema deltas found: 0` / `Schema evolution policy intact.`
- `devtools test tests/unit/storage/test_index_fast_forward_lifecycle.py tests/unit/storage/test_index_fast_forward_executor.py`: the two tests this fix targets (`test_current_index_schema_has_a_complete_delta_declaration`, `test_schema_policy_rejects_an_index_bump_without_a_delta_declaration`) now pass. Two unrelated pre-existing failures remain (`test_nonsemantic_delta_without_operations_is_rejected`, `test_delta_without_a_declared_class_is_rejected`) -- confirmed via `git stash` to already fail identically on master, caused by a separate latent bug where `invalid_versions` flags every declaration with `version > current_version` regardless of the v40 gap. Out of scope here.
- `mypy --strict polylogue/storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py`: no issues
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched file: clean
- `devtools render all --check`: no drift
- `devtools verify --quick` (pre-push hook): passed

body:
Currently, every .intent config change requires running `tachyon intent build` then `go build` to bake the new config into the binary. This makes the proxy harder to deploy in containers and impossible to reconfigure without a full rebuild cycle.

`loadRuntimeConfig()` in `cmd/tachyon/main.go` parses .intent files at startup via the existing `intent.ParseFiles()` code path. If no .intent files exist, it falls back to `cur.LoadConfig()` (the current baked-in behavior). Zero behaviour change for existing users who don't touch .intent files.

body:
## What changed

- correct self-play value targets by recording the player-to-move and preserving draws as zero
- version replay buffers and isolate remediated data/checkpoint paths from invalid legacy artifacts
- enforce piece geometry, king safety, flying-general rules, and no-legal-move termination
- apply the KL-driven learning-rate multiplier to Adam
- make replay-buffer writes atomic and reload rolling buffers by producer iteration
- add CPU-safe AMP behavior, a working PyQt UI, UI asset sets, and reproducible dependencies
- add an automated color-balanced checkpoint evaluator and permanent remediation log
- add nine regression tests for training targets, schema validation, and Xiangqi legality

## Why

The archived replay buffers were inspected and all 24,182 records in the main buffer had a value target of `-1`. The previous collection code labeled every position using the terminal `current_player` and converted draws into losses. Existing checkpoints therefore cannot be treated as evidence of model quality.

Move validation also accepted geometrically invalid direct moves, did not reject positions leaving the moving general attacked, and did not terminate on checkmate or stalemate. In addition, the configured ten-ply limit ended opening games before useful long-horizon learning.

## Impact

New runs use schema-v2 buffers under `data/remediated_v1` and checkpoints under `models/remediated_v1`. Legacy buffers and checkpoints remain historical artifacts and are deliberately rejected by the repaired pipeline.

Model improvement is not claimed by this PR. New self-play, retraining, and frozen-checkpoint evaluation are still required.

## Validation

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 9 tests passed
- bytecode compilation passed for all Python entry points
- real PyTorch forward and optimizer smoke test completed with finite outputs
- uniform-vs-uniform evaluator smoke test completed with alternating colors and zero illegal actions
- schema-v2 atomic save and same-length rolling-buffer reload were verified
- 20 random legal-game stress runs completed without exceptions or action-map failures

author: jorgensandhaug
body:
## Summary

- keep the latest `onDraftApplied` callback in a ref so live session/policy callback churn cannot recreate `loadDraft`
- stop callback-only rerenders from refiring the initial composer-draft load effect
- preserve one initial read per session target plus explicit `reloadDraft()` and relevant `user.message` / `session.queue.changed` event reloads
- add a patch changeset for `@opengeni/react`

## Production evidence

During the 2026-07-27 production incident, two 1 GiB API replicas were OOMKilled at 11:26:32Z and 11:28:34Z. Their preserved previous containers served 14,078 successful composer-draft GETs in about 13 minutes; draft reads were 84–85% of API traffic, approximately 1,500–1,982 requests/minute near the incident.

The regression reproduced the source amplifier before the fix: an inline `onDraftApplied` callback caused a draft read, state update, new callback identity, new `loadDraft`, and another initial-load effect until the test timed out at 5 seconds. body:
Pass 3 of the Pause & Segmented Rides epic ([ROH-100](https://linear.app/rohun/issue/ROH-100)). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-segmented-rides-pause-design.md`, decisions D2, D3, D5. Plan (revision 3, with both review gates recorded): `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-schema-v6-segments-backfill.md`.

Rides now persist their pause boundaries and their paused total. No rider-visible behavior changes — the pause control itself is Pass 4.

## What lands

**`RideSchemaV6` redeclares `RideRecord`** rather than mutating `RideSchemaV2`'s class. V3, V4 and V5 all list that class, so adding a property there would retroactively rehash four versions and leave an on-disk V5 store matching no schema in the plan. The entity name stays `RideRecord`, so CloudKit keeps its record type; the `RideRecord` typealias moves to V6 and V2 is marked frozen.

**`segmentsData`** — optional (nil is how "not backfilled" and "synced from a V5 device" are representable) and `@Attribute(.externalStorage)`, because `summaries()` fetches every row and an inline ~300 KB blob is the ROH-64 fault. Guarded on the attribute itself in `SchemaInvariantTests`, since a sidecar file appears either way.

**`pausedSeconds`** on the record and on `RideSummary`, denormalized beside `movingTimeSeconds`.

**Dual-write, degrading read.** `trackData` and `thumbnailData` keep their flat shape and stay complete for V5 builds reading the same records. Reads prefer `segmentsData` and fall back to the flat track when it is absent, corrupt, or when the flat blob is empty — never throwing on a bad blob.

**The backfill is a background sweep, not a migration stage.** This deviates from D2 and from the issue, with PO sign-off. `didMigrate` runs inside `ModelContainer.init`, which `AuraApp.init()` calls before the first frame: a reviewer measured 0.043 s per three-hour ride, so ~16 s for a 365-ride history, and a throw there fails the container — which `AuraApp` catches by falling back to an in-memory store that reads as an empty History and overwrites the widget snapshot. A stage also runs once, while V5 devices keep syncing down rows with `segmentsData` nil, so only something re-runnable can ever make `trackData` retirable. `RideSegmentBackfiller` is a `@ModelActor` doing the same work off the launch path, budgeted at 50 rows per launch, cancelled when a ride starts.

## Review

Two three-reviewer adversarial gates (skeptic / architecture / product, refuting mandate). The first killed revision 1's design before any code; the second, against the finished diff, found that the sweep was still running on the main thread — `@ModelActor`'s executor serializes on whatever thread enqueues it, and a `Task {}` inside a SwiftUI `.task` inherits MainActor isolation. Also fixed from that gate: batch saves silently reverting a concurrent writer's columns (reproduced), `maxRows` budgeting rows examined so corrupt rows starved the rest, an empty `trackData` being stamped as a permanently-empty ride, and several comments asserting things the code did not support. Full table at the end of the plan.

Five sweep guards were verified by mutating the source and watching the specific test fail.

## Verification

- `swift test --package-path AuraCore` — 691 tests, 142 suites, green (three consecutive runs; two `@Model` classes now share the entity name `RideRecord`, the ROH-65 hazard, so every container suite holds the serial gate and `RideStoreTests` moved to Swift Testing to take it).
- `swiftlint --strict` — clean.
- `Aura` scheme builds for the iPhone 17 simulator.

## Before this ships — PO action required

**Promote the CloudKit production schema.** [ROH-108](https://linear.app/rohun/issue/ROH-108), filed as a release blocker with the console path. V6 adds `CD_segmentsData` and `CD_pausedSeconds` to `CD_RideRecord`; production schema is immutable from the client, so a V6 build shipped before promotion cannot export at all and sync stops for every V6 user with no in-app error surface. This blocks TestFlight, not just the App Store.

**Known unverifiable here.** That a V5 build ignores an unknown `CD_segmentsData` and degrades to a flat track cannot be tested in this repo — macOS CI has no CloudKit entitlement. Needs two-device verification, which should also check what the V5 device pays: the sweep dirties historical rows, so the history re-exports and re-downloads.

**Costs taken on knowingly.** Dual-write roughly doubles per-ride storage on device and in the rider's iCloud quota until `trackData` retires ([ROH-109](https://linear.app/rohun/issue/ROH-109), filed with a trigger). Every End tap now encodes the track twice on the main actor; Pass 4 measures that on device alongside the pause flush ([ROH-101](https://linear.app/rohun/issue/ROH-101)).

**Residual, documented rather than hidden.** A row dirty during a save can still lose a concurrent writer's columns — per-row saves shrink the window to the save itself, and SwiftData exposes no merge policy to close it; the reachable writer is the CloudKit import context. And `segmentsData` is derived once: a V5 device that finishes a ride after a V6 device backfilled its partial track pins that ride to the fragment. A 24 h settling window keeps it narrow; closing it fully needs a derivation marker, i.e. another column and another promotion.

author: jjgroenendijk
body:
## Context

Two inputs drove this work: the Anthropic context-engineering article (lightweight, progressively disclosed agent instructions) and the [OKF v0.2 spec](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md), which gives a concrete format for that while staying plain markdown in git.

Before this, snippets were bare markdown: no description, tags, status, or provenance for the app to search, filter, or display. Categories were capped at one directory level, which forced prefix-named siblings like `git-commits` / `git-workflow`. Nothing showed what a selection costs in context.

## Change

Snippets

- `snippets/` is now a conformant OKF v0.2 bundle. All 58 concept documents carry `type`, `title`, `description`, `tags`, `status`, and `generated`; rules derived from external docs also carry `sources`.
- `generated.at` comes from each file's last content-changing commit, not the migration date, so freshness signals stay truthful.
- Types stay descriptive: `Rule` for prescriptive rules, `Playbook` for procedures, `Reference` for source material.
- Directories nest: `code/{quality,powershell,scripts}`, `git/{commits,workflow}`, `docs/{agents-md,project-docs}`, `knowledge/okf`, `platform/intune`. All moves use `git mv`.
- `writing-caveman` merged into `writing`. Overlap between individual rules stays a user decision, so no conflict detection was added.
- `knowledge/okf` rules updated from v0.1 to v0.2: `timestamp` and the body `# Citations` list are noted as read-only fallbacks, and two new rules cover the trust/provenance and attested-computation families.
- Generated `index.md` per directory (SPEC §8), with `okf_version` in the bundle root (SPEC §12).

App

- `lib/frontmatter.js` splits frontmatter from body and derives trust tier and staleness. Parsing is permissive per SPEC §11: malformed YAML degrades to body-only rather than throwing.
- `lib/tree.js` builds a nested category tree; `CategoryFilter` renders it recursively, and selecting a parent selects everything below it.
- `lib/output.js` owns output assembly, shared by the preview, the copy button, and the new token meter so all three measure the same string. Nested paths render as `## Code / Quality`.
- Token budget meter in the output header: estimated tokens and a bar against the new `ui.tokenBudget` (default 2000), amber when over. The estimate is chars/4 on purpose and labeled approximate — a static export has no tokenizer and the real count varies by model.
- Snippet previews prefer the frontmatter description; badges appear only for a non-stable status or a stale concept.
- Search now matches description, tags, and category path.

Tooling and docs

- `pnpm check:okf` validates conformance, wired into pre-commit and CI. The loader is permissive by design, so this is what turns silent metadata loss into a failed commit.
- `pnpm snippets:index` regenerates the bundle indexes.
- `snippets/AGENTS.md` (plus `CLAUDE.md` symlink) documents the bundle; the root guide and `docs/requirements.md` are corrected.

## Impact / Risk

- Snippet ids are file paths, so ids and edit URLs change. Nothing persists a selection, so no stored state breaks.
- `content` is body-only, so frontmatter cannot leak into copied output — asserted in an e2e test.
- `index.md` files are committed, so they need regenerating with `pnpm snippets:index` after adding or moving a rule.

## Incidental fix

E2E could not run at all before this branch: Playwright targeted `http://localhost:3000` while the app serves under the basePath from `config.yml`, so the readiness check 404ed and timed out. The theme specs also still asserted the Nord palette replaced in 6493aaf. Both are fixed, and `tests/rule-selection.spec.js` adds coverage for nested categories, the meter, and frontmatter-free output.

## Tests

```
cd app
pnpm lint          # clean, --max-warnings 0
pnpm test          # 70 passed
pnpm check:okf     # 78 files checked, conformant
pnpm build         # static export OK
pnpm test:e2e      # 9 passed
```

Screenshot of the result in `docs/screenshots/okf-nested-categories/`.

## Not included

Raised during planning, deliberately deferred: JSON/raw export for agents, shareable selection URLs, skill-bundle export, per-snippet strictness tags, and `log.md`.

body:
Adds a three-state (system / light / dark) theme to the Subscription Billing Runner, with no flash before hydration and cross-tab synchronization.

## What changed

- **Spec first.** `docs/frontend.md` gains a `## Theme` section defining the preference values, the `subscriptions:theme` storage key, the always-concrete `data-theme` attribute, the pre-paint requirement, cross-tab propagation, and the explicit non-goal that theme never touches SSE, the store, or any server route.
- **`src/features/theme/`** (new): `theme.ts` (pure logic — parse/resolve/cycle), `theme-script.tsx` (blocking inline `<head>` script), `use-theme.ts` (client hook), `theme-toggle.tsx` (three-state control in the dashboard header).
- **Semantic tokens** in `src/app/globals.css`: light values on `:root`, dark on `[data-theme="dark"]`, exposed as Tailwind utilities via `@theme inline`. Intermediate names (`--border-subtle`) avoid colliding with Tailwind's namespace.
- **Full migration** of the ~140 hardcoded color utilities across `constants.ts`, `formatters.ts`, the 9 dashboard components, and `dashboard.tsx`. The `transaction-card` enter-flash keyframe moved off raw hex and unified on `emerald`.

## Design decisions

**The token collapse is intentionally lossy.** `text-slate-500/600/700` all became `content-muted`; `bg-amber-50` and `bg-amber-100` both became `warn-surface`. Some elements shift by one shade. That is the point of a token system — no extra tokens were invented to preserve every original shade.

**`slate-950` was disambiguated by role, not find-and-replace.** `focus:border-slate-950` on inputs is a focus affordance → `border-strong`. `border-slate-950 bg-slate-950 text-white` on selected/primary controls is an inverted surface → `surface-inverted` / `content-inverted`.

**`hover:bg-slate-800` on the primary button became `hover:opacity-90`,** since a single darker-slate hover does not invert correctly across both themes.

## Deviations from the plan — please read

**1. The plan's theme script alone did not survive hydration. Added a fix (`aa61c3f`).**

The plan assumed `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` would let the inline script's `data-theme` stand. It does not: React reconciles the *server-rendered* `data-theme="light"` back onto `<html>` during hydration, and `suppressHydrationWarning` only suppresses the console warning, not the attribute patch. Because `use-theme.ts` as specified called `applyPreference` only when the preference was `system` (or on a `storage` event), an explicit `light`/`dark` preference was silently reverted on every load.

Measured with Playwright against a production build, stored preference `dark`:

```
before fix:   at commit: dark   after load: light
after fix:    at commit: dark   after load: dark
```

Fix: the mount effect in `use-theme.ts` now re-asserts `applyPreference(preference)` for *every* preference before deciding whether to subscribe to the media query. This is the same approach `next-themes` uses. The pre-paint guarantee is unaffected — the inline script still wins the initial paint, which the `waitUntil: "commit"` e2e assertion covers.

**2. Added one token the plan's table omitted: `--color-scrim`.**

The pause dialog backdrop is `bg-slate-950/45` — a *third* meaning of `slate-950` that the Migration Hazards section did not list. Applying the table literally (`surface-inverted`) turned the modal scrim into a **light** wash over the dark page: the backdrop brightened instead of dimming. A scrim must darken in both themes, so it cannot invert. `--color-scrim` is defined once on `:root` as `var(--color-slate-950)` with no dark override. This is a distinct semantic role, not a shade-preservation token.

**3. `vitest.setup.ts` needed a `matchMedia` stub.**

jsdom does not implement `window.matchMedia`, so mounting the header in `dashboard.test.tsx` threw once `ThemeToggle` was added. Added a guarded light-mode stub (only applied when `window` exists and the API is missing).

**4. Updated an existing assertion in `dashboard.test.tsx`.**

It asserted the literal classes `bg-amber-50` / `bg-slate-50` on transaction cards; retargeted to `bg-warn-surface` / `bg-surface-muted`.

**5. Collapsed a now-redundant ternary** on the pause dialog's custom-seconds input, whose two branches became character-identical after migration.

## Contrast pass (Task 9)

Computed WCAG ratios from the actual Tailwind oklch palette rather than estimating:

| Pair (dark) | Ratio | |
|---|---|---|
| `content-muted` on `surface` (slate-400/slate-900) | 6.79:1 | AA |
| `content-subtle` on `surface` (slate-500/slate-900) | 3.74:1 | AA (secondary/large) |
| `content` on `surface` | 16.28:1 | AA |
| `warn` / `success` / `danger` content on their surfaces | 8.15–12.03:1 | AA |

**No token values were changed.** The plan's conditional remedy (lightening `content-subtle` and shifting `content-muted` to slate-300) was not triggered: `content-subtle` is used only for secondary text and a decorative dot separator, and 3.74:1 clears the 3:1 bar the plan set for secondary text. `content-muted` at 6.79:1 clears 4.5:1 comfortably.

**Pre-existing issue, not introduced here and not fixed here:** in *light* mode, `content-subtle` on `surface` (slate-400 on white) is **2.63:1**, below even the 3:1 secondary bar. This is the original `text-slate-400` in `transactions-panel.tsx`, carried over unchanged so light mode keeps its current appearance. Worth a follow-up.

## Verification

- `yarn test` — 62 passed, including 8 new in `theme.test.ts`
- `yarn test:e2e` — 7 passed, including 3 new theme specs (persistence across reload, pre-hydration application, cross-tab sync)
- `yarn build` and `yarn lint` clean
- Palette-utility grep over `src/` returns nothing; no raw hex in `src/`
- No new dependencies; no `tailwind.config.js`
- `grep -i theme` over `src/server/`, `src/shared/`, `src/app/api/` returns nothing — theme never reaches SSE, the store, or a server route
- Visually checked in a production build, both themes: subscription cards, pause dialog, create form, notices, transaction feed including the flash animation, and the danger/cancel controls

body:
## What

The flight track is now coloured by altitude with a legend showing the range it spans, and hovering either view marks the same moment in the other. Hovering the barogram moves a marker along the track; hovering the track marks the point on the chart. Arrow keys, Home, End and Page keys drive the same thing from the keyboard, and the chart announces elapsed time and altitude as a slider rather than a static image.

## Why

The track was a flat blue line, which threw away the altitude axis that was already in every point of the KML. A pilot looking at a climb on the chart had no way to see where over the ground it happened.

## How it works, and two things worth knowing

MapLibre cannot style a line from a per vertex data property. `line-gradient` is the only mechanism that varies colour along one line, and it keys exclusively to `line-progress`, which MapLibre computes itself as normalised distance along the rendered geometry. So the ramp is precomputed as explicit stops: each stop pairs a point's position along the full track with the colour for its altitude.

Those fractions must be measured against the full geometry, not the decimated stop set. The decimated path chords straight across every thermal circle and comes out 40 percent shorter, which displaces colours by kilometres.

Hover identity is an index into the full track, not `secondsFromStart`. Seconds are not unique: the parser falls back to the array index when the KML seconds list is short, and colliding values make the two views resolve the same hover to points tens of kilometres apart.

## How to test

pnpm run check

The two browser scripts need a running dev server, so they are not in that aggregate:

pnpm exec tsx scripts/verify-track-gradient.mts
pnpm exec tsx scripts/verify-track-hover.mts

Closes #14

body:
## Summary
- `ExportButton` and `SessionExportSheet` both cleaned up an exported conversation file by deleting `url.deletingLastPathComponent()`. That's safe today only because `ConversationExporter.resolveDirectory` happens to mint a unique per-export temp subdirectory — an invariant that lived only in a comment. `ConversationExporter.export(...)` is public and already accepts a `directory:` override; a host that passes its own directory and copies this cleanup idiom (as `SessionExportSheet` literally did — its comment says "mirroring `ExportButton`'s pattern") would recursively delete a directory it doesn't own.
- Make ownership representable on `ShareableFile`: it now carries `ownedDirectory` (the directory the exporter itself created — `nil` when the caller supplied their own `directory:` override) and exposes `cleanup()`, which removes only what the exporter actually created. Both view call sites now call `file.cleanup()` and never compute a path to delete themselves.
- `cleanup()` uses `do`/`catch` + `Log.persistence` instead of `try?` (AGENTS.md Principle 6 / `SilentCatchAuditTest`).

**Is this fixing a live bug?** No in-repo caller currently passes `directory:` to `ConversationExporter.export(...)` — both `ExportButton` and `SessionExportSheet` use the default temp path. So `cleanup()`'s nil-`ownedDirectory` branch (the one that matters — "don't delete a caller-owned directory") is exercised only by the new unit tests, not by a live production caller today. This is a public-contract fix closing a latent hazard in a public API, not a fix for a bug users were hitting. It's still worth shipping now: `ConversationExporter.export(directory:)` has been public since before this PR, so the hazard is live for any external consumer of the API today, even though no in-repo caller trips it yet.

## API surface
- `ShareableFile` gets a new public member: `cleanup()`. Diff against `origin/main`'s `Tests/APIFreezeTests/api-surface-baseline/ManifoldRuntime.txt` is a single-line addition.
- `ownedDirectory` and the 4-arg `init(...ownedDirectory:)` are `package`, not `public` — the only construction site is `ConversationExporter` itself (same module), so there's no cross-package consumer, and a public setter would let a host mint a `ShareableFile` with an arbitrary `ownedDirectory` and hand it to `cleanup()`, reopening the exact recursive-delete-of-an-unowned-directory bug this PR closes, one layer up (nothing validates `ownedDirectory` is an ancestor of `url`).
- Kept the old 3-parameter `init(url:suggestedFilename:contentType:)` public and explicit — the api-surface digester flags a defaulted-parameter addition to an existing initializer as "constructor removed" (it keys on the full parameter list), so relying on a default alone would have broken the freeze gate.

## Housekeeping
- `.gitignore`: the existing `scripts/dx-walkthrough/runs/**` negation pattern (added after a prior 2.9GB accidental commit) unintentionally re-included any `.build/` a walkthrough run happens to build under `app/.build/`. Concretely: `git add -A` on the run tree already sitting untracked in this checkout (`2026-07-25_v0.73.0_live-20260725/`) would stage up to 42 `.build/checkouts/*` dependency clones as broken embedded-git-repo gitlinks (git warns `adding embedded git repository` per clone — these are real nested `.git` repos, so it's gitlink references, not full file trees, but still 42 unfetchable references no clone of this repo could resolve), plus the intentionally-tracked `.md` summaries. Added an explicit `scripts/dx-walkthrough/runs/**/.build/` re-ignore after the negation block; verified with both a synthetic test tree and a dry-run `git add -n` against the real leaked directory that `.build/` content is ignored again while curated `.md` summaries stay tracked, and that the fix reduces `git add -n`'s output from 42 embedded-repo warnings + 50 staged paths down to 8 (just the `.md` files).

## Ride-along fix found during review
- `SessionExportSheet.performExport()` re-runs on every format-picker change (`.task(id: selectedFormat)`) and was overwriting `exportedFile` without cleaning up the previous export — every format switch orphaned a `ManifoldKit-export-<uuid>/` temp directory nothing ever removed. Now calls `cleanupExportedFile()` before starting the next export. Pre-existing bug, not a regression from this PR's changes, but the PR's whole subject is "who cleans up the export directory" so this is the right place for it.

## Tests
- `test_cleanup_removesExporterOwnedTempDirectory` — exporter-minted temp directory is removed by `cleanup()`.
- `test_cleanup_doesNotDeleteCallerSuppliedDirectory` — the important case: a caller-supplied `directory:` (and a sibling file placed in it) survives `cleanup()` untouched; only the exported file itself is removed. Verified this test is capable of catching the regression it guards: temporarily reproduced the old `deletingLastPathComponent()` behavior in `cleanup()` and confirmed the test fails against it, then restored the real implementation.
- `test_repeatedExport_cleanupBeforeReplace_leavesNoOrphanedDirectory` (new, in `SessionExportIntegrationTests`) — covers the `SessionExportSheet` ride-along fix through the service layer, since the view's private `.task` lifecycle isn't independently hostable in the existing snapshot-only UI test suite.
- Dogfooded `cleanup()` in `test_export_useDefaultDirectory_writesToTemp`'s own fixture teardown, replacing its last remaining `try? removeItem(at: deletingLastPathComponent())`.

## Test plan
- [x] `swift build --target ManifoldUI`, `swift build --target ManifoldRuntime` — call-site + demotion changes compile
- [x] `swift build --build-tests` — full test target compiles
- [x] `swift test --filter ConversationExporterTests` — 15/15 pass
- [x] `swift test --filter SessionExportIntegrationTests` — 7/7 pass
- [x] `scripts/api-surface-baseline.sh --check --modules "ManifoldRuntime ManifoldUI"` — clean after baseline regen; diff vs `origin/main` is a single-line addition
- [x] Reviewed by an independent skeptical-reviewer pass; findings applied (public-surface demotion, `.gitignore` prose correction, `SessionExportSheet` ride-along fix, honest liveness note)

body:
## What

A 5-day **"Data Detectives"** science week for **grades 1–2** with a heavy focus on **making and interpreting graphs**, narrated by Dot the Ladybug (a tiny "data detective").

**Causal arc:** observe & count → record data in a table → show data as a pictograph → show & read data as a bar graph → run a full experiment and graph the results.

Each day is hands-on: kids collect their own data (a counting hunt, a **Ramp Race**, a **Paper Airplane Contest**), graph it, and then read what the graph says (most / least / how many more / how many altogether).

## Why a renderer change

None of the existing HTML worksheet kinds can draw a graph, and content fields are HTML-escaped — so a week about graphing couldn't show a graph to read or a grid to plot on. This PR adds two new kinds to the shared `worksheet_html_renderer.py` (also usable by the API weekly-plan flow):

- **`barGraphWorksheet`** — axed, titled plot with countable gridlines. *Blank* mode = student colours bars from their data; *pre-filled* mode = student reads the bars. Optional interpretation questions.
- **`pictographWorksheet`** — keyed picture graph with per-symbol scaling (e.g. each 🐛 = 2). *Blank* (draw) and *pre-filled* (read) modes. Optional questions.

Standards touched: CCSS.Math **1.MD.C.4** & **2.MD.D.10** (represent & interpret data); NGSS K–2 practices (analyzing/interpreting data, fair tests).

- `src/worksheet_html_renderer.py` — two new render fns + CSS + dispatch entries (additive; existing kinds untouched).
- `tests/test_html_graph_worksheets.py` — 6 tests (blank/pre-filled bar graph, scaled pictograph, dispatch registration, value clamping).
- `scripts/generate_data_week_series.py` — the week generator (student packet + embedded teacher guide). Output dir is gitignored; the script fully reproduces the week.

- `venv/bin/python scripts/generate_data_week_series.py` → 15 pages, exit 0.

## Summary
- Resume PDF uploads on the deployed sandbox threw `ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined` in production while working identically locally — root-caused via `vercel logs` (not guesswork).
- `pdf-parse` pulls in `pdfjs-dist`, which evaluates `new DOMMatrix()` at module scope and tries to polyfill it on Node via a native `@napi-rs/canvas` dependency. That polyfill is wired up through a `require()` constructed dynamically deep inside pdfjs-dist's own bundle — invisible to Vercel's build-time file tracer, so `@napi-rs/canvas` silently never made it into the deployed function bundle. Locally this was fully masked because Bun implements `DOMMatrix` natively.
- Replaced `pdf-parse` with [`unpdf`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/unpdf), which is purpose-built for serverless/edge runtimes and mocks canvas internally instead of needing a real native polyfill — this removes the whole bug class at the source rather than patching around it (no native binary dependency, no dependency on the bundler tracing a hidden `require()` correctly).
- Updated `README.md`/`WALKTHROUGH.md` to reflect the new library, and logged the incident + fix in `docs/deployment-journal.md`.

author: iloveleon19
body:
Fixes #107750.

## What Problem This Solves

`capEntryCount` computes a removable budget and then slices the removal list at it:

```ts
const maxRemovableEntries = Math.max(0, maxEntries - preservedCount);
...
const toRemove = sorted.slice(maxRemovableEntries);
```

When the preserved population alone reaches `maxEntries` the budget clamps to `0`,
and `sorted.slice(0)` returns **every** removable key. At that point the pass stops
meaning "trim the surplus" and starts meaning "no unpreserved entry may exist":

- the `toSorted` by `updatedAt` becomes dead code — an entry written microseconds
  ago is removed exactly like a 47-day-old one;
- the store still exceeds `maxEntries` afterwards, because preserved entries are
  unremovable by construction, so the next write runs the same doomed pass again;
- that is the per-write `capped session entry count {"removed":1,...}` churn in the
  issue, but the churn is the symptom — the deletion of live sessions is the damage.

The issue asks for exactly this: *"Cap enforcement should detect `exempt-count >=
maxEntries` and stop re-running a pass that cannot succeed."*

Two things in the codebase already point the same way:

- `capEntryCount` is documented as able to exceed the cap in this situation, with a
  test named *"can temporarily exceed the cap when every candidate is runtime-protected"*.
  That only holds today when there is nothing removable at all; the moment one
  transient entry appears it is destroyed, and the store still exceeds the cap.
- `wouldCapActiveSession` already models the budget-`0` state explicitly and treats
  it as "the active unprotected session would be the one removed" — the warning path
  knows about the condition that the deletion path does not guard.

## What this does

Neither extreme is right in the unsatisfiable state. Deleting every removable
entry destroys live sessions and still leaves the store over the cap; skipping
the pass entirely leaves a configured positive `maxEntries` with no count-based
behavior at all.

`capEntryCount` now resolves its budget through a shared helper:

```ts
function resolveRemovableEntryBudget(maxEntries: number, protectedCount: number): number {
  const budget = Math.max(0, maxEntries - protectedCount);
  if (budget > 0 || maxEntries <= 0) {
    return budget;
  }
  return Math.min(maxEntries, MIN_OVER_CAP_REMOVABLE_ENTRIES);
}
```

| state | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| budget > 0 | trims to budget | unchanged |
| **budget == 0** | **deletes every removable entry** | keeps the newest `min(maxEntries, 25)`, still trims the rest |
| `maxEntries <= 0` | deletes everything removable | unchanged |

So count-based retention stays active and bounded in exactly the state where it
used to be destructive, and the surviving removable population is never allowed
to exceed the operator's configured cap. Age-based retention is untouched either
way, because `pruneStaleEntries` applies `pruneAfter` before this runs.

`wouldCapActiveSession` — the predicate behind the "your active session is about
to be capped" warning — now resolves its budget through the same helper, so the
warning and the deletion path cannot disagree about what a pass would remove.

## Relationship to #104137

#104137 fixed the adjacent problem — maintenance deleting sessions that are actively
working — by preserving every identity covered by an active session-work admission.
That protects a session which *already holds* an admission. It cannot protect the
window before one exists: run prep writes the entry, a maintenance pass triggered by
an unrelated session write deletes it, and the admission then finds nothing to claim.

This was verified rather than assumed: the admission machinery is present in the
build where the failures below were observed (`beginSessionWorkAdmission` is in the
shipped runtime), and the cron sessions still died. The two fixes are complementary.


## This is not a 2026.7.1 regression

Worth stating up front, because the loudest symptom is new even though the defect
is not. Comparing the shipped bundles of the two releases:

| symbol | 2026.6.11 | 2026.7.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `maxRemovableEntries = Math.max(0, maxEntries - preservedCount)` | present | present |
| `slice(maxRemovableEntries)` | present | present |
| `capped session entry count` | present | present |
| `beginSessionWorkAdmission` | **absent** | present |
| `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` | **absent** | present |

The deletion behavior is byte-identical in both, and the git history agrees: the
preserve-based budget landed 2026-04-23 and thread-scoped preservation 2026-05-02,
both well before 2026.6.11 — which is also the version #107750 was originally
reported against.

What 2026.7.1 added is the *check*. `beginSessionWorkAdmission` (#98510) validates
that the session row is still the one the run started with, so a deletion that used
to pass unnoticed now aborts the run. The check is correct; it surfaced a
pre-existing silent loss. The fix belongs on the deletion side, which is what this
PR does — not on loosening the new validation.

The cron flow's own inability to survive row loss is filed separately as #114573;
it is a distinct concern, because any other cause of row loss produces the same
total failure there.

## Evidence

### Live failure, OpenClaw 2026.7.1, Mattermost + Codex gateway

`sessions.json` held **622 entries — 618 thread-scoped + 4 group/channel-scoped**,
i.e. 100% preserved, against the built-in default `maxEntries` of 500
(`session.maintenance` was never configured). Budget = `max(0, 500 - 622) = 0`.

Cron session keys (`agent:main:cron:<uuid>`) match no preserve rule. Run prep created
the entry, a maintenance pass on an unrelated session write deleted it, and
`beginSessionWorkAdmission`'s `assertAllowed` took the `!currentEntry` branch:

```
CronSessionLifecycleClaimError: Session "agent:main:cron:<uuid>" changed
while starting work. Retry.
```

**All 3 cron jobs, 5 consecutive days, dying 215–428ms into `cron-setup`** — inside
the create → verify window. The payloads never ran once.

Raising `maxEntries` above the preserved count stops it immediately, which confirms
the budget is the trigger. That is a workaround the operator has to discover; this
patch removes the cliff, which returns as the preserved population keeps growing.

### After-fix live run, over-cap state reproduced on purpose

Same gateway, `session.maintenance.maxEntries` temporarily lowered from 2000 to
**100** so the protected population (694) exceeds it and the budget resolves to
the floor, `min(100, 25) = 25`. All timestamps UTC, from the live gateway log.

**Count-based trimming stays active** — the store was reduced to the floor rather
than left unbounded, and the protected population was untouched:

```
02:01:17  maxEntries 2000 -> 100, gateway restarted
02:21:30  [sessions/store] capped session entry count
02:23:49  [sessions/store] capped session entry count
02:23:50  [sessions/store] capped session entry count

store before:  total 772   protected 691   removable  69
store after:   total 718   protected 694   removable  24     <- floor is 25
```

**A cron run survives a maintenance pass inside its create → claim window** —
this is the failure mode from the report, reproduced deliberately:

```
02:29:39  cron run enqueued (isolated agent turn, delivery disabled)
02:29:43  [sessions/store] capped session entry count      <- pass fires mid-run
02:29:50  run finished
```

```json
{
  "action": "finished",
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "CAP-FLOOR-PROOF-OK",
  "runId": "manual:f7041f46-…:1785205780598:1",
  "durationMs": 10244,
  "deliveryStatus": "not-requested",
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 23564, "output_tokens": 13 }
}
```

No `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` was emitted. The cap pass at 02:29:43 landed
four seconds into the run — the same window that previously killed every run —
and the session row survived it because the run's freshly written entry is inside
the floor.

body:
## What & why

`yaml.Unmarshal` silently ignores unknown YAML keys in `quack.yaml`. When a config key is renamed (e.g. `memory_role` → `memory.bucket`), deployments that drift to the old key get no signal: the server boots clean, agents run, and the feature is broken with nothing to diagnose.

This replaces `yaml.Unmarshal` with stream-based decoding using `yaml.NewDecoder().KnownFields(true)`, so any unrecognized YAML field at **any nesting level** now fails startup, naming the unknown key. For known renames (`memory_role`), a pre-scan on the raw YAML produces a migration hint: `"unknown field 'memory_role' — use memory.bucket instead"`.

Closes #560

## Spec (non-trivial changes)

- **Scope / out of scope** - In scope: KnownFields enforcement for all config keys, `knownRenames` map + pre-scan helper for migration hints. Out of scope: bulk migration tooling for existing deployments.
- **Forbidden actions** - Do not add new dependencies; keep `yaml.v3` only. Do not modify `applyDefaults()` — structural validation (KnownFields) and semantic validation (applyDefaults) remain separate concerns.
- **Output contract** - `Load()` returns an error naming the unknown field; for known renames, the error appends a replacement hint. No fields are silently ignored anymore.
- **Test cases** - unknown top-level key rejected; unknown nested key in server/workspace/gates.judge rejects; deprecated `memory_role` rejects with migration hint mentioning both old and new keys; valid config with all legal fields loads without regression; KnownFields applies at every nesting level.

- [x] `go test ./...` passes (`-race` for concurrency changes)
- [x] `make vet && make fmt` clean
- [ ] Frontend (if touched): N/A — no frontend changes
- [x] Changed `openapi.yaml`? No — this is config parsing, not API contract

- [x] Comments say what the code *can't* - no narration or change history

body:
Der Hero-Look aus Variante A („Nebel") — nicht mehr als eine große Fläche oben, sondern als **Containerelement**, aus dem sich die ganze Startseite baut.

**Reines Mockup.** In der App ist nichts davon verdrahtet, kein `js/`-Modul und kein Stylesheet der App wurde geändert.

👉 <https://daimpad.github.io/mosh-school/mockups/startseite-muster.html>

## Der Vorschlag: eine Regel, kein Look

Das Bild ist ein **Signal für die Art des Ziels**, nicht Dekoration. Je weiter unten auf der Seite, desto funktionaler der Bereich — und desto weniger Bild. Wer die Seite zum zweiten Mal sieht, findet Werkzeuge schneller, weil sie anders aussehen als Orte.

| Ebene | Behandlung | Warum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marke | Bild, groß | der einzige Ort, an dem Atmosphäre allein zählt |
| Welten (Instrumente, Genres) | Bild | Orte, in die man eintaucht und die einen eigenen Klang haben |
| Wege (Können, Thema, Spielziel, Training) | nur Motiv | Struktur statt Stimmung — hier entscheidet man, statt zu stöbern |
| Werkzeuge | flach, nur Icon | wird bedient und wiedergefunden; ein Hintergrund macht das Icon nur schwerer erkennbar |
| Verweise | Zeile mit Icon | führt woanders hin |

## Zum Spielen

- **Vier Rhythmen** umschaltbar: nach Ebene (Vorschlag) · Bild nur als Akzent · alles mit Bild · heutiger Stand ohne Bild
- Regler für Weichzeichnung, Deckkraft, Sättigung; Themenwechsel dunkel/hell/auto
- Bildwahl: je Kachel ein anderes oder eines für alle, „durchtauschen", Drag & Drop
- Schalter „Blur unabhängig von der Größe" — macht einen der beiden Befunde unten sichtbar

## Zwei Befunde aus dem Verkleinern

Der Hero-Look überträgt sich **nicht** unverändert auf Kachelgröße. Beides ist gelöst und im `CSS zum Übernehmen`-Block der Seite dokumentiert:

1. **Blur muss mitskalieren.** 18 px Weichzeichnung lassen eine 116 px hohe Kachel zu einem Farbfleck zusammenfallen — auf 300 px Hero-Höhe nicht. Der Blur hängt jetzt an `--blur-faktor` (h2 `.68`, h3 `.5`).
2. **Der Scrim muss dichter werden.** Der Hero-Scrim läuft erst ab 62 % Höhe an; auf Kachelhöhe steht der Titel dadurch fast im Bild und verschwindet im hellen Thema. Kacheln bekommen einen dichteren Verlauf, das große Marken-Element behält den weichen.

Die unveränderte Bildebene aus Variante A bleibt wie gewählt:

```css
.genre-landing-bg {
  position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none;
  background: center / cover no-repeat var(--hero-bild);
  filter: blur(18px) saturate(.4);
  opacity: .35;
  transform: scale(1.18);   /* Überzoom: sonst zieht der Blur helle Ränder herein */
}
```

## Änderungen

- **neu** `mockups/startseite-muster.html` — die Mockup-Seite
- `mockups/hintergrundbilder.html` — Link auf die neue Seite
- `images/bg/README.md` — beide Mockup-Seiten aufgeführt

Die Seite nutzt die echten Stylesheets, das echte Motiv-SVG (`motivSvg`) und die echten Instrument-Symbole (`domaeneIcon`) der App — sie zeigt also, wie es wirklich aussähe, nicht wie eine Nachbildung aussieht. Bildquelle wie beim Hero-Vergleich: `images/bg/bilder.json` zuerst, Verzeichnislisting als Rückfall, Drag & Drop jederzeit; Fehler erscheinen auf der Seite statt nur in der Konsole.

## Verifikation

`validate.py` · `build_grafiken.py --check` · `lift.py` + `build_index.py` ohne Diff · `build_bg_index.py --check` — alle sauber.

Playwright gegen eine GitHub-Pages-Simulation (Unterpfad `/mosh-school/`, 404 auf Verzeichnislistings):

- keine Konsolen-Fehler, keine HTTP-Fehler ≥ 400
- kein horizontaler Überlauf bei 1280 px und 390 px
- alle vier Rhythmen bauen (28 Kacheln; Bildkacheln 11 / 4 / 16 / 0)
- alle 21 Bilder geladen, je Kachel ein anderes; Regler, Blur-Kopplung, „durchtauschen" und Bildwahl nachweislich wirksam
- beide Themes gerendert, keine leeren Icons, keine leeren Titel

body:
## Kanzlei-Cross-Tenant-Scope: `service_typ='komplett'` → echtes Mandat (`kanzlei_faelle`)

**Befund (RLS-Runtime-Test 27.07., prod):** `test-kanzlei` sah **15/20 claims + 15/39 leads + 8/15 fall_dokumente** bei nur **3 Mandaten**.

**Wurzel:** 6 SELECT-Policies (`claims__b1sel_au`, `faelle_claim_bridge_select`, `leads__b1sel_au/_an`, `timeline__b1sel_au/_an`) + der Helper `claim_sichtbar_fuer_aktuellen_user` scopen den **kanzlei-Zweig auf `service_typ='komplett'`** (= der Kunde hat das Voll-Paket gekauft, trifft auf 21/22 Claims zu) statt auf **`kanzlei_faelle`** (= diese Kanzlei wurde für diesen Fall mandatiert). `claims` hatte zwar einen `is_kanzlei_member`-Check, aber der Backfill setzte **allen 21 Claims dieselbe Kanzlei** → Check immer `true`.

**Heute latent** (nur 1 Kanzlei existiert → kein aktiver Cross-Tenant-Leak), **aktiver Breach beim 2.-Kanzlei-Onboarding**. Defense-in-depth vor dem Onboarding.

**Fix (Migration `20260727120255`, via Supabase-Plugin):**
- Kanonischer Helper **`is_kanzlei_mandat(claim_id)`** (SECURITY DEFINER, `kanzlei_faelle`-Join auf `profiles.kanzlei_id`) — ein SSoT statt 6× inline-Prädikat.
- `claim_sichtbar_fuer_aktuellen_user` kanzlei-Zweig → `is_kanzlei_mandat` (fixt zugleich `fall_dokumente` + den ersten Bridge-Zweig, die delegieren).
- **Surgical `ALTER POLICY`** auf den 6 Policies — **nur der kanzlei-Zweig** ändert sich, alle anderen Rollen-Zweige byte-verbatim erhalten.
- Keyt auf `kanzlei_faelle` → die `claims.kanzlei_id`-Überzuweisung wird RLS-irrelevant, **kein Daten-Backfill nötig**.

**Verify (RLS-Cross-Tenant-Harness gegen prod, nach Apply):**
| Rolle | claims | leads | fall_dokumente |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kanzlei vorher** | 15 | 15 | 8 |
| **Kanzlei nachher** | **2** | **2** | **0** |
| Kunde | 5 → 5 | 0 | 3 → 3 |
| SV | 2 → 2 | 2 | 2 → 2 |
| Dispatch | 0 → 0 | broad | broad |

→ Kanzlei auf ihre Mandate gescoped; **kunde/sv/dispatch unverändert** (keine Kollateral-Rolle betroffen).

**Follow-ups (separat, nicht security-kritisch):** Portal-Query (`mandate/page.tsx`/`kanban/page.tsx`) von `faelle_claim_bridge`+`service_typ` auf einen `kanzlei_faelle`-Loader umstellen; `claims.kanzlei_id`-Backfill kosmetisch korrigieren; `/kanzlei/fall/[id]`-Detail-View bauen (404).

Reine RLS-Migration, kein App-Code. `ALTER POLICY` (kein `CREATE` → kein rls-policy-gate-Ratchet).

Die Golden-Schlüssel aller Erlasse dieses Kantons, die über HTM/ZH/PDF erschlossen sind, fielen damit weg, obwohl ihre Snapshot-Dateien unter `public/normtext/kanton/` unangetastet blieben. Der `§8`-Wächter des Zweigs griff ebenfalls nur je Kanton und war für einen routen-beschränkten Lauf zu grob.

Dass ein Kanton mehrere Routen hat, ist keine Theorie — Routen-Inventar empirisch ausgelesen:

| Route | Kantone |
|---|---|
| LexWork | AG AI **AR** BE BL BS **FR** GL **GR** **LU** NW OW **SG** SH SO TG UR **VS** ZG |
| HTM | GE NE **TI** |
| ZH-PDF | ZH |
| PDF | **AR** **FR** **GR** JU **LU** **SG** SZ **TI** VD **VS** |

Fett = in zwei Routen, also von diesem Defekt betroffen.

## Belegter Schaden

Commit `7a14fa06` (23.6.2026, `npm run normtext -- --nur=kanton --kanton=AR --discovery`) löschte die **59 Golden-Schlüssel** von `public/normtext/kanton/AR-1203.json` — «5945 insertions, 59 deletions». AR-1203 ist ein PDF-Routen-Erlass (olexAt-Profil, `ar.clex.ch/api/de/versions/1203/pdf_file`), war und ist registriert (`register.json` `artikelAnzahl` 59). Allein seine Drift-Basis (§7 lit. d) verschwand.

Wiederhergestellt wurde der Bestand in PR #389 (`e288e683`) durch Reprojektion; die **Ursache** im Generator blieb dort ausdrücklich unangetastet. Dieser PR behebt sie.

## Repro-Beweis rot → grün

**Vor dem Fix** — die Merge-Logik wurde zuerst unverändert (ALT-Semantik) nach `scripts/normtext/golden-kanton-merge.ts` extrahiert, damit der Fehlschlag isoliert sichtbar wird. `npx vitest run src/tests/golden-kanton-merge.test.ts` → **exit 1**, 4 von 9 Tests rot:

```
 ❯ src/tests/golden-kanton-merge.test.ts (9 tests | 4 failed)
     × Discovery-Teillauf (nur LexWork) LÄSST die PDF-Routen-Schlüssel des Kantons stehen
     × ALT-Logik verlor genau diese Schlüssel — der Defekt ist hier festgenagelt
     × Vollauf mit WEGGEFALLENEM Artikel purgiert innerhalb des Erlasses weiter
     × Mehrere Ziel-Kantone: nur die gefahrenen Erlasse werden ersetzt

AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'sha-ar-1203-1'
```

**Zusätzlich Ende-zu-Ende, gegen den echten Golden** (55'823 Einträge, kein Netz): simulierter `--kanton=AR --discovery`-Lauf-Index = alle AR-LexWork-Schlüssel *ohne* `kanton/AR/1203/*` (6327 Einträge), ALT-Merge angewandt, Ergebnis in eine Sandbox geschrieben (`public/` symlinkt, Repo-Golden unberührt), `check-golden-normtext.ts` darauf:

```
Variante ALT — Bestand 55823 · Lauf-Index 6327 · Ergebnis 55764 · AR/1203 im Ergebnis: 0

  FEHLER: 59 Snapshot-Knoten OHNE Golden-Eintrag (1 Datei(en)) — diese Artikel haben keine Drift-Basis (§7 lit. d):
    public/normtext/kanton/AR-1203.json (59): kanton/AR/1203/art_1, kanton/AR/1203/art_1.1, …
check:golden-normtext ROT   (exit 1)
```

Das ist der Schaden von `7a14fa06` exakt nachgestellt: −59, genau diese Datei.

**Nach dem Fix**, identische Eingabe:

```
Variante NEU — Bestand 55823 · Lauf-Index 6327 · Ergebnis 55823 · AR/1203 im Ergebnis: 59

check:golden-normtext OK — 55823 Snapshot-Knoten vollständig im Index, keine Waisen   (exit 0)
```

Das NEU-Ergebnis ist **byte-gleich** zum committeten `golden/normtext-snapshot.json` (`diff` → nur der Abschluss-Newline des Simulations-Skripts). Unit-Tests: 9/9 grün.

## Wie der Purge-Umfang jetzt bestimmt wird

`scripts/normtext/golden-kanton-merge.ts:79-83` (`istErsetzbar` in `mischeGoldenKanton`):

```ts
const istErsetzbar = (key: string): boolean => {
  const p = erlassPraefix(key);
  return p !== null && kantone.has(p.split('/')[1]) && frischePraefixe.has(p);
};
```

Granularität = **Erlass-Präfix** `kanton/<KT>/<lawIdSafe>`, also genau eine Snapshot-Datei (`erlassPraefix`, Zeile 22). Die ersetzbaren Präfixe werden aus dem **Lauf-Index abgeleitet**, nicht aus den CLI-Flags: der Lauf-Index enthält genau die neu erzeugten Knoten und sagt damit selbst, welche Routen liefen — ein künftiger Teillauf-Schalter kann die Frage nicht mehr falsch beantworten. Ein Erlass mit 0 Knoten in diesem Lauf (nicht gefahrene Route, Fetch-Fehler, leere Extraktion) behält seinen Altbestand und wird als `§8`-Zeile gemeldet (`normtext-snapshot.ts:1054-1064`).

Die **Purge innerhalb** eines ersetzten Erlasses bleibt erhalten: weggefallene Artikel-Schlüssel (Anker-Rename, Anhang-Reorg) fallen weiterhin weg — sonst verwaisen sie und `check:golden-normtext` (Prüfung b) wird rot. Ein eigener Test nagelt das fest.

`--nur=zh` nutzt jetzt dieselbe Regel (`normtext-snapshot.ts:952`). Für einen gesunden ZH-Lauf ergebnisgleich (ZH wird nur über die ZH-PDF-Route erschlossen, der Lauf liefert also jeden ZH-Erlass), schliesst aber dieselbe Fehlerklasse: der pauschale `!k.startsWith('kanton/ZH/')`-Purge hätte bei einer ganz oder teilweise fehlgeschlagenen ZH-Phase den Altbestand der nicht gelieferten Erlasse still gelöscht — dort sogar ohne jeden Erfolgs-Wächter. Deklarierte Änderung, Richtung §8.

## Verhaltensneutralität des Vollauf-Pfads

**Argument:** liefert der Lauf jeden Erlass des Ziel-Kantons, dann ist jedes Erlass-Präfix dieses Kantons in `frischePraefixe` — die Präfix-Bedingung fällt mit der alten Kantons-Bedingung zusammen, und `gemischt` ist Schlüssel für Schlüssel dasselbe. Die Logiken divergieren **genau dann**, wenn ein Erlass des Ziel-Kantons im Lauf fehlt — also genau im Teillauf-Fall, der der Defekt ist.

**Beleg 1 (Test):** `src/tests/golden-kanton-merge.test.ts` führt die ALT-Implementierung wörtlich als Referenz mit und vergleicht mit `toEqual`:
- Vollauf-Index (alle Routen inkl. AR-1203) → `neu` **identisch** `alt`, und zwar mit dem frischen Stand.
- `§8`-Fall «Ziel-Kanton ohne einen einzigen frischen Eintrag» → `neu` identisch `alt` (der alte `erfolgKantone`-Wächter griff hier schon).

**Beleg 2 (empirisch):** NEU-Merge gegen den echten 55'823-Golden → byte-gleich zum committeten Stand (s. oben).

| Tor | Exit | Ergebnis |
|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc -b` | 0 | ok |
| `npm run lint` | 0 | 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning (`src/components/suche/useUniversalSuche.ts`, unberührt) |

## What & why

Design for the last two `symbol-placement: line` parity gaps — chain **phase**, and line-label **collision extent** — which share one root: X-GIS decides both in SCREEN space, MapLibre decides both in the tile's frame. Follows #1358, #1370 and #1383, which closed the gaps that did not need a frame change.

**Docs only. No production code.** The first increment was implemented and measured, and the measurement refuted the design's central rule — so the code is reverted and the refutation is the most valuable thing here.

## How it works

The document's load-bearing claim was that we do not need tile-local units to get MapLibre's invariant: `forEachLineLabelPolyline` already hands the label pass **mercator metres**, sliced per tile, so each polyline's first vertex is a camera-invariant origin. Walk from there with the existing `spacingPx / pxPerMeter` step and the #1358 cadence is untouched while the phase becomes a property of the data.

I built that, unit-proved the invariance (a clipped run's anchors stay a subset of the full run's — impossible for the screen walk), and then measured it against the reference:

| | shield 1 | shield 2 | shield 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MapLibre | (22, 428) | (329, 322) | (636, 216) |
| X-GIS, screen walk (`main` today) | (18, 428) | (325, 324) | (632, 218) |
| X-GIS, walking from vertex 0 | (176, 374) | (484, 272) | (791, 164) |

**~4 px off became 155 px off.** The offset is uniform across the chain, so the cadence is intact and #1358 is unaffected; 155 is about half the on-screen step (~325 px). That signature says the origin is right in kind and the half-step convention is wrong — MapLibre's `getAnchors` offsets by the label's own length rather than a fixed `spacing / 2`, and walks tile-clipped geometry whose vertex 0 is not ours.

So §3.0 now opens with the refutation, the measured table, three ranked leads, and an instruction to derive the convention from **measured MapLibre anchor positions** (the `_debug-ml-collision-boxes.spec.ts` harness already exposes them) instead of assuming it. The rest of the document — the four increments, the §5 risks (off-screen walk cost, the #1050 phantom-chord rule, collision cost, test churn), the §6 verification posture — stands.

Camera invariance on its own is not worth a 155 px regression against the reference. The two have to arrive together, so nothing is wired.

body:
Implements the durability contract decided in #126. **A workbook that loses its vectors now says so.**

## The problem it closes

Before this, a workbook that passed through Numbers or LibreOffice was *indistinguishable* from one that never had embeddings. Those tools rebuild the archive and drop every `xl/zlsxEmbeddings/*` part — parts removed, not merely unreferenced — so the caller silently got nothing back. ~200 bytes of provenance in a carrier that survives the rebuild turns that into a detectable, attributable state.

| | |
|---|---|
| `pkg/recovery_record.zig` | codec + carrier extraction (std-only, own test target) |
| `Workbook.setEmbeddings` | writes both carriers |
| `Workbook.embeddings()` | reads them back |

## The accessor is now a tagged union

```zig
pub const EmbeddingState = union(enum) {
    present:  EmbeddingView,   // vectors here
    stripped: RecoveryRecord,  // vectors gone, provenance recovered
    absent,                    // never had any
};
```

This is the API expressing the contract. Collapsing `.stripped` into a bare `null` would leave the default caller experience silent — which is exactly what the contract rejects — so the call-site churn is the point, not a cost. `viewOrNull()` exists for callers that have already decided how to treat a strip; the name says the state is being discarded.

## End-to-end validation

Against the tools that motivated the whole thing. In every case the vectors are **genuinely destroyed** (index and workbook rel gone) and the provenance still comes back:

| Round-trip | Vectors | Record | Carrier that answered |
|---|---|---|---|
| LibreOffice Calc 26.2.3.2 | destroyed | **recovered** | `defined_name` |
| openpyxl 3.1.5 | destroyed | **recovered** | `defined_name` |
| LibreOffice, then `docProps` removed (Document Inspector) | destroyed | **recovered** | `defined_name` |
| LibreOffice, then defined names removed | destroyed | **recovered** | `doc_props` |

The last two rows are why there are two carriers rather than one: each is independently sufficient and their removal mechanisms don't overlap — Document Inspector ▸ Document Properties strips `docProps` and never touches defined names.

## Reading it back is the hard part

The carriers are rewritten by the very tools the record exists to survive. All three normalizations measured in #126 are handled, and **each would silently lose the record** if the parser matched its own writer's bytes:

- `hidden="1"` comes back as `hidden="true"` — both valid `xsd:boolean` lexical forms
- the payload comes back XML-escaped: `"x"` → `"x"`
- the element gains `function="false"`, `vbProcedure="false"`

So `findDefinedNameValue` matches on `name=` rather than tag shape, and guards the preceding byte so `codeName=` can't match `name=`.

## Wire format

One pipe-separated ASCII line; every text field percent-encoded. Stricter than the separator needs, deliberately — it also guarantees the payload survives XML escaping (no `<` `>` `&` `"`), Excel formula-string quoting (no `"` to double), and any consumer that re-encodes text (pure ASCII, no UTF-8 to mangle). A test asserts the encoding of a deliberately hostile model name contains none of those bytes.

Chunks across numbered names (`_zlsxRecovery0`, `1`, …) against the ~255-char practical limit, rather than truncating — a truncated provenance record is worse than none, because it reads as authoritative.

## Two things worth reviewing closely

**Upsert, not append.** A second `setEmbeddings` clears both the staged defined-name plan and any chunks already in the saved bytes. Without it, `addDefinedName` surfaces `DuplicateDefinedName` on the second call, and two generations of chunks concatenated by index decode as garbage. Test pins both.

**A malformed record reports `.absent`, not an error.** It's provenance, not data — it must not make an otherwise readable workbook un-openable.

## Gates

- `zig build test` — 61/61 steps, **1649/1649** (main 1589)
- `zig build test-corpus` — 10/10, 33/33
- emb-4 and emb-4B harnesses rebuilt against the new accessor; `emb4-verify` now reports whether a strip was silent or recorded

Unblocks **E5** (Python): the binding now has three distinguishable states to expose.

author: fawadyolo
body:
## Problem

On mobile the hero video took **11.4s to appear — but only ~1.5s of that was downloading it.**

The clip was JS-assigned behind `window.addEventListener('load', ...)` plus a `requestIdleCallback`. That put it behind the entire analytics stack. Measured on emberandiron.pk at 375×812:

```
7,487ms  DOMContentLoaded
7,972ms  ├─ googletagmanager gtag/js ×2
8,433ms  ├─ facebook fbevents.js (103 KB)
9,106ms  ├─ doubleclick / analytics / merchant-center beacons
9,777ms  └─ gtag cascade ends
9,883ms  load event fires
9,895ms  ◄── video request STARTS (12ms after load)
11,420ms video downloaded → first frame
```

The original comment said the defer was so the clip "doesn't block the initial page load" — reasonable intent, but `preload="none"` already handled that. The `load` gate was pure dead time, and it scaled with however slow the ad stack was that day.

## Changes

**1. Hand source selection to the preload scanner** — replaces the JS `data-src` assignment:

```html
<source src="…hero-mobile.mp4" media="(max-width: 760px)" type="video/mp4">
<source src="…hero-1080.mp4" type="video/mp4">
```

Support for `media` on `<source>` was verified with a test page rather than assumed — both directions select the correct render **and never fetch the other one**. Had it been unsupported, phones would have silently pulled the desktop file.

**2. `preconnect` to `cdn.shopify.com`** so the video host's DNS+TCP+TLS isn't paid cold on the critical path.

**3. Fixed drift between `index.html` and the theme.** `index.html`'s hero JS never received the mobile-source branch that `theme.js` had, so it served the 1920×1080 landscape file into a 375×617 portrait box — 66% of every frame cropped, including the "EMBER & IRON" plate. Both files now share identical hero logic.

**4. Retry refused autoplay** on first interaction or tab refocus, guarded so it won't fight the scroll-pause. iOS Low Power Mode blocks autoplay even when muted; the old code swallowed the rejection behind a `started` flag with no recovery path.

## Verification

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile file | `hero-1080.mp4` ❌ | `hero-mobile.mp4` ✅ |
| Mobile poster | desktop crop ❌ | portrait ✅ |
| Fetch start (local) | 264ms | **24ms** |
| Desktop | — | `hero-1080.mp4`, no wasted fetch ✅ |
| Console | — | no errors ✅ |
| JS syntax | — | `node --check` passes both files ✅ |
| Drift | index vs theme differ | identical ✅ |

## Not in scope

Video file size is untouched. A 720×1280 re-encode (1.78 MB → 0.36 MB, SSIM 0.993) is a separate call — worth making after measuring this change on a real phone on mobile data, since that's where the remaining download cost actually bites.

## After merge

Deploy the theme, then re-measure live. The local 24ms understates the win; the real change is that the fetch no longer waits 9,883ms for gtag and the Facebook pixel.

author: korrnals
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug in the ADR 0005 streaming timeout implementation. The connect timer reused the main `AbortController`, which broke retry — all retry attempts failed instantly because the signal was already aborted.

## Bug

When the connect timer fired (30s), `controller.abort()` marked the main signal as aborted **permanently**. `withRetry` tried to retry, but `fetch(url, {signal: abortedSignal})` immediately failed with `AbortError`. All 3 retry attempts wasted in <1ms. User saw "connect timeout after 30000ms" even though retry should have attempted a fresh connection.

## Fix

Each retry attempt now creates its own `AbortController` for the connect timer. The main controller (caller cancel / maxDuration / inactivity) is wired to abort the attempt controller via `addEventListener('abort')`, but the attempt controller is fresh per-retry. `ConnectTimeoutError` is retriable; cancel/maxDuration `AbortError` is not.

## Test

New regression test: mock `fetch` to hang for attempts 1-2 (connect timer aborts per-attempt signal → `ConnectTimeoutError` → retried), resolve on attempt 3. Assert: `onDone` fires, `fetch` called 3 times. This test would FAIL with the old bug (all 3 attempts abort instantly).

## Verification

- `npm run compile` — clean
- `npm test` — 322 passing (321 + 1 new regression test)
- `bash scripts/local-ci/run-all.sh` — 9/9 gates green

PR #24 머지 직후 재측정에서 규칙 파일의 수치 두 개가 어긋난 걸 발견했어요.

| 항목 | 문서값 | 재측정 |
|---|---|---|
| `E501` | 436건 | **439건** |

Story 5.2가 테스트와 SQL을 추가하면서 벌어진 차이예요. 숫자만 갈아끼우면 다음 스토리에 또 어긋나니, **수치의 성격을 나눠서** 처리했습니다.

## 관측값 → 규모만 남김

코드가 늘면 같이 늘어나는 값입니다. 이 수치들의 용도는 "이건 소음이니 켜지 마라"는 근거일 뿐이라 정확한 건수는 의미가 없어요.

- `backend.md`: 기본 룰셋/`E501`/`S101` 건수 → "수십 건"·"수백 건"
- `backend.md`: `S608` "7건" → 건수 삭제 (오탐이라는 사실만 남김)
- `ruff.toml`: `E501` "436건" → "수백 건", `UP017` "29곳" → 건수 삭제

## 불변량 → 그대로

유지해야 하는 목표값이라 드리프트하면 안 되는 것들입니다. 손대지 않았어요.

- ruff 검출 **0건** — 뜨면 새로 생긴 것이라는 계약
- RLS 정책 **0개** — deny-by-default 설계(AD-7)

## 트립와이어 → 남기고 의도를 명시

SQL 조각 빌더 호출부 **6곳**은 일부러 정확한 숫자로 남겼어요. 이건 소음 근거가 아니라 **안전성의 근거**라서, 숫자가 달라지면 그 자체가 신호여야 합니다.

`slot_taken_sql` · `free_doctor_sql` · `occupied_sources_sql`이 안전한 이유는 "호출부 6곳이 전부 리터럴 인자"이기 때문이고, 강제하는 장치는 없어요. 실제 호출부가 6곳이 아니면 새 호출자가 생긴 것이므로 인자부터 확인하라는 주석을 달았습니다. Story 5.3(워크인)이 네 번째 호출자를 추가할 예정이에요.

## 검증

- 머지된 main 기준 `ruff check .` → **0건** 유지 (ruff.toml 주석만 변경이라 동작 영향 없음을 확인)

## Summary

Implements the refined "Zero-Cost In-Country AI" plan: replaces the paid Anthropic API with a self-hosted Ollama container and Upstash Redis with a Postgres-backed rate limiter, so the AI assistant (FAQ, quota projection, antibiotic suggestion, pathway check) can run at zero recurring cost with patient data staying on the clinic's own VPS.

- **Stock correctness fix** — `src/lib/stock.ts` standardizes every page (FMS/MO dashboards, Index, Terimaan, DoctorRequest, PharmacistFulfilment, RefillWalkinDialog, DrugLedger's current-balance summary) on one sort-before-fold, SET-semantics helper, fixing a real bug where FMS/MO could silently disagree with the rest of the app on a drug's current stock.
- **Rate limiting** moves from Upstash Redis (fails open on outage) to a Postgres RPC (`ai_rate_limit_hit`, fixed window, fails closed).
- **`_shared/llm.ts`** wraps a self-hosted Ollama instance (generate / streaming / grammar-constrained JSON with retry + deterministic fallback / health check), replacing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` in all three edge functions.
- **`pathway-check`** becomes fully rule-based against a small NAG 2024 pathway table (seeded from `knowledge-service`'s vault notes) — no LLM call, <100ms instead of ~25s.
- **FAQ retrieval** (`_shared/faq.ts`) answers how-to-use-the-app questions with deterministic IDF-weighted matching; only the loosest-match tier ever calls the model.
